missing: ATS907 had public model data: Hsu & Kengatharan, ARVO 2011, 'Safety and Efficacy of a Novel Topical Rho Kinase Inhibitor ATS907 in Normotensive Cynomolgus Monkeys' (https://iovs.arvojournals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2360870): single-dose IOP -3.7/-4.65 mmHg vs -2.43 latanoprost, plus a rabbit abstract. The draft's note says 'no public model data' for ATS907; this is wrong. The Phase 2 failure (NCT01520116 status unknown, NCT01668524 no results) is known only from the Wang & Chang 2014 review, so it is not scorable without a tier 1-5 patient source. If one is found, ATS907 would be a contra on a normotensive-monkey IOP model.

DE-104 Phase 2 trials NCT00650338, NCT00657579, NCT00656240, NCT00868894 are registered with no posted results. The discontinuation for a missed primary endpoint (late 2010) appears only in the review; no Santen tier 5 document was found in budget, and no DE-104 model data was found.

Ripasudil (K-115, Kowa; approved Japan 2014) is a ROCK inhibitor for POAG/OHT with its own rabbit/monkey IOP models (e.g. Isobe 2014, Curr Eye Res) and Japanese patient trials (Tanihara 2013, Am J Ophthalmol); no track if it is in the class. Not verified in budget.

AR-12286 (Aerie's earlier ROCK inhibitor) had monkey IOP data and a Phase 2 patient trial (Williams 2011, Am J Ophthalmol) before netarsudil; a member drug's own model with no track. Not verified in budget.

Sovesudil (PHP-201) Phase 3 in POAG/OHT, NCT04863365 (pH Pharma, completion 2023-11, status unknown, no posted results); no result found in a Firecrawl search. If it reports, it sets the patient side of the nzw-rabbit-iop-sovesudil efficacy and safety track above the 2013 tier 5 release.

AR-12286 (Aerie ROCK inhibitor) patient IOP result, ARVO 2010 (Williams, IOVS 51:1633, https://iovs.arvojournals.org/article.aspx?articleid=2370306; NCT00902200) precedes every model in this tile, which makes the netarsudil and sovesudil engagement/efficacy tracks retrodictions.
rule_questions: ROCKET-1 (Study 301) failed its primary endpoint, which was non-inferiority of mean IOP to timolol, although IOP fell significantly. The model predicted IOP lowering with no comparator margin. Does an active-comparator NI primary that fails while the absolute endpoint responds count as an efficacy 'contra', or is it untested for the model? The draft kept it as a status-neutral patient_trial.

Decision 16 margin_stated: the 2017 PharmR states NOAEL margins of 8x/2x for the chronic studies but a corneal-haze NOEL margin of 1. Is margin_stated judged on the NOAEL or on the most sensitive finding? Neither margin was shown to be public before Phase 2. Status 'same' holds either way.

When the system relied on is an IOP-lowering model in normotensive animals, should a failed sibling-member drug with model data only in a conference abstract (ATS907 ARVO 2011) be admissible on the model side (tier 1 needs DOI/PMID)?

efficacy 4: an undirected genotype hypothesis ('may influence response') meets an underpowered null (aOR 1.31, CI 0.42-4.10). Is that a failed prediction (contra) or no patient result (untested)? The rules decide neither undirected predictions nor underpowered nulls outside terminated trials.

Tanihara 2008 (PMID 18332309) showed IOP lowering with the ROCK inhibitor SNJ-1656 (Y-39983) in healthy volunteers, before every model in this tile was public. Does a healthy-volunteer IOP result count as a prior 'patient result' for the retrodiction rule (efficacy 2/6, engagement IOP-linked readouts)? Scored here as not, since the rule says patient result.

Engagement retrodiction: the AR-12286 prior patient result (2010) was IOP, not the engagement readout (outflow facility/EVP, first measured in dosed humans 2017). Does any prior patient result on the target make an engagement model retro, or only one on the same readout? Checked literally as retro (engagement 2/4/6/8).
